questions.prompt: This function replaced a conditional that chose between EffectDspVolumeUpdate or EffectApVolumeUpdate based on device type and offload state. Now both are called unconditionally and SUCCESS is always returned. What is a consequence of ignoring the return values of EffectDspVolumeUpdate and EffectApVolumeUpdate?

options.label: If EffectDspVolumeUpdate internally fails, the error is silently swallowed and EffectApVolumeUpdate still runs.
EffectApVolumeUpdate will crash because EffectDspVolumeUpdate already consumed the shared_ptr.
The function now deadlocks because both inner functions lock dynamicMutex_.
Nothing changes because both functions were always called before too.

questions.explanation: The old code did ret = EffectDspVolumeUpdate(...) or ret = EffectApVolumeUpdate(...) and returned ret. The new code calls both without capturing or checking their return values, so any error from either is lost and the caller always sees SUCCESS. Both functions take a shared_ptr by value (copy), so no use-after-free; and they lock inside themselves, not on the caller's dynamicMutex_.
questions.reinforce: Correct — the old conditional return value is now discarded, masking inner failures.

questions.prompt: GetSystemVolumeWithDeviceType has a three-tier fallback: (1) exact device+stream, (2) SPEAKER device+stream, (3) this final return 0.5f. The unit test GetSystemVolumeWithDeviceType_Fallback_002 calls this with STREAM_ALARM and DEVICE_TYPE_EARPIECE (neither set). What value does the test assert, and does the comment in the test match the code?

options.label: Test asserts 0.5f; the test's own comment says "should return default 1.0f" — comment and code disagree.
Test asserts 1.0f; the comment and code agree.
Test asserts 0.0f because no volume was ever set.
The test would fail because the function throws on unknown device types.

questions.explanation: The code returns 0.5f as the final fallback. The test EXPECT_EQ(0.5f, result) passes, but its own desc comment reads "should return default 1.0f" — a mismatch between the documented expectation and the actual hardcoded fallback. The non-enhanced SystemVolumeMap_ defaults to 1.0f for STREAM_MUSIC, so 0.5f is an inconsistent default.
questions.reinforce: Correct — the hardcoded 0.5f fallback is inconsistent with both the test comment and the 1.0f default used in SystemVolumeMap_.

questions.prompt: After the if/else block in CheckExistAudioEffectChainInner, there is a return false; statement. Can this line ever be executed?

options.label: No — both the if and else branches return, so the trailing return false; is unreachable dead code.
Yes — if IsEnhancedRoutingSupported() throws an exception, control falls through to return false;.
Yes — when Util::IsEnhancedRoutingSupported() returns a value other than true or false.
No — but the compiler will remove it automatically so it's harmless to keep.

questions.explanation: IsEnhancedRoutingSupported() returns a bool, so the if/else covers all paths and both branches return. The return false; after the closing brace can never execute. A compiler may warn about unreachable code, and it indicates a copy-paste artifact from refactoring.
questions.reinforce: Correct — it's unreachable dead code left over from the refactor.

questions.prompt: When UpdateCollaborativeState is called with the same isCollaborationEnabled value as the current state (no state change), what side effects still occur before the early return?

options.label: collaborationRouteMode_, sinkInfo_.isCollaborationEnabled, and sinkInfo_.collaborationRouteMode are all updated even though the collaboration state itself didn't change.
Nothing is updated — the function returns SUCCESS immediately without touching any member.
Only isCollaborationEnabled_ is reassigned to the same value; sinkInfo_ is untouched.
The function returns ERROR because the state is unchanged.

questions.explanation: The assignments to collaborationRouteMode_, sinkInfo_.isCollaborationEnabled, and sinkInfo_.collaborationRouteMode happen before the if (isCollaborationEnabled_ == isCollaborationEnabled) check. So even when the collaboration state is unchanged, the route mode is still propagated. This is intentional — the route mode can change independently of the collaboration state — but it's subtle: calling UpdateCollaborativeState(CLOSE, MCH_ROUTE_MODE) after being in CLOSE state still updates the route mode.
questions.reinforce: Correct — the route mode is always propagated, even on a no-op collaboration state change.

questions.prompt: The old code iterated sceneTypeToSessionIDMap_ and constructed a key (it->first + "_&_" + GetDeviceTypeName()) to look up sceneTypeToEffectChainMap_, returning ERROR if the key wasn't found. The new code iterates sceneTypeToEffectChainMap_ directly. Under EnhancedRouting (multiple effect chains per scene type, one per device), why is the old key-construction approach broken?

options.label: GetDeviceTypeName() returns only the global deviceType_, so it can't construct device-specific keys for the multiple per-device chains that exist under EnhancedRouting.
sceneTypeToSessionIDMap_ is empty under EnhancedRouting, so the loop body never executes.
The string concatenation produces a key with the wrong separator character.
Iterating sceneTypeToEffectChainMap_ directly is slower and causes a timeout.

questions.explanation: Under EnhancedRouting, sceneTypeToEffectChainMap_ contains keys like sceneType_&_effectMode_&_deviceName (per-device chains), but the old code built keys as sceneType_&_GetDeviceTypeName() using the single global deviceType_. That key wouldn't match any per-device chain, causing a false return ERROR. Iterating sceneTypeToEffectChainMap_ directly avoids the key mismatch entirely.
questions.reinforce: Correct — the global deviceType_ can't address per-device effect chains under EnhancedRouting.

questions.prompt: This code runs when sceneType_ == "SCENE_COLLABORATIVE". If the constructor is called with the default parameter value COLLABORATION_INVALID_ROUTE_MODE, what happens to tempEffectBuffer_, directOutput_, and collaborativeOutput_?

options.label: Neither branch is taken — all three remain nullptr, which will cause DoProcess to fall through to the silence-write else branch.
tempEffectBuffer_ is created as a safety default because INVALID is treated like MCH.
directOutput_ and collaborativeOutput_ are created because INVALID is treated like DEFAULT.
The constructor asserts and aborts because INVALID is not a valid collaboration route mode.

questions.explanation: COLLABORATION_INVALID_ROUTE_MODE matches neither MCH nor DEFAULT, so the if/else-if chain falls through without creating any buffer. In DoProcess, the MCH branch checks collaborationRouteMode_ == COLLABORATION_MCH_ROUTE_MODE (false) and the DEFAULT branch checks collaborationRouteMode_ == COLLABORATION_DEFAULT_ROUTE_MODE (false), so execution reaches the final else that writes silence. The node is effectively a no-op pass-through in this state.
questions.reinforce: Correct — INVALID route mode leaves all buffers null, making the node a silence-writing pass-through.
